candidate_relations.label: Dyshidrotic eczema
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical presentation (violaceous annular patches in axilla, no blisters, negative Wood lamp) and biopsy (lymphocytes obscuring dermal-epidermal junction = lichenoid interface dermatitis) are incompatible with dyshidrotic eczema, which features vesicles on acral surfaces and spongiotic histology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Dyshidrotic eczema is a vesicular dermatitis of palms/soles/lateral digits, not axillary violaceous annular patches with lichenoid interface histology

candidate_relations.label: Mycosis Fungoides
candidate_relations.reason: While MF can mimic lichen planus clinically and histologically (interface infiltrate), it is a neoplastic T-cell lymphoma with distinct immunophenotypic and molecular features. The presentation of well-circumscribed violaceous annular patches with classic lichenoid interface histology in a single axillary site is more consistent with inverse lichen planus. MF is a related differential but an incompatible final diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Mycosis fungoides is a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma that can present with patches/plaques and lichenoid histology but represents a distinct neoplastic entity rather than inverse lichen planus

case_quality_flags: Histology description (lymphocytes obscuring DEJ) is classic for lichenoid interface dermatitis supporting lichen planus; MF cannot be fully excluded without immunohistochemistry and T-cell clonality studies, which are not reported
